question: Shared: prediction of MCI-to-AD conversion within 3 years (MCI-c vs MCI-nc; pMCI vs sMCI) from baseline structural MRI in ADNI MCI. P-207 (Liu et al., Front Neurosci 2022) uses VBM grey-matter volume organised by ICA-derived networks into a two-level coupled representation, classified by AdaBoost with linear-SVM base learners. P-185 (Li et al., BioMed Res Int 2021) uses FreeSurfer regional cortical thickness and volume projected into a subspace learned on AD/NC data, classified by a linear SVM. Features, classifier, subject subsets and scanners differ, which condition 1 allows. The ledger's 'EEG/MEG' modality for P-207 is wrong: both papers are T1 sMRI only.
metric: Accuracy in both. The ledger's P-207 figure (90.44%) is its AD-vs-NC accuracy. P-207's printed conversion accuracy is 87.72%, and that figure is used here.

figures.P-207: MCI-c vs MCI-nc accuracy 87.72% (sens 84.16%, spec 91.64%), 10-fold CV, 234 subjects (126 MCI-c/108 MCI-nc); no interval printed. Wilson with n = 234: z^2/n = 3.8415/234 = 0.01642; centre = (0.8772 + 0.00821)/1.01642 = 0.8711; half-width = 1.96*sqrt(0.8772*0.1228/234 + 3.8415/(4*234^2))/1.01642 = 0.0422; 95% CI [0.829, 0.913]. The 87.72% is the best of 15 (E1, E2) settings of the same CFMnetwork model (range 70.24%-87.72%). Other feature representations in the paper: OFMROI 64.15% (Wilson [0.578, 0.700]), OFMnetwork 68.62%, best CFMROI 75.10%.
figures.P-185: pMCI vs sMCI accuracy 69.37% (sens 75.39%, spec 61.23%, AUC 0.6951), 10-fold CV repeated 20 times, 221 subjects (126 pMCI/95 sMCI); no interval printed. Wilson with n = 221: z^2/n = 0.01738; centre = (0.6937 + 0.00869)/1.01738 = 0.6904; half-width = 0.0603; 95% CI [0.630, 0.751]. Original morphological features (no subspace learning): 62.92% (Wilson [0.564, 0.690]).

matched_figure_check: No figure in either paper is reported under the other's condition. The headline figures already share horizon (3 years), single baseline timepoint, contrast and cohort family, and neither paper evaluates the other's feature pipeline. The nearest common-condition figures are the plain regional-feature baselines, and they agree closely: P-207's OFMROI 64.15% [0.578, 0.700] and P-185's original morphological features 62.92% [0.564, 0.690]. P-207's own Table 3 therefore places its 23.6-point gain in its two-level coupled representation, reported at the best of 15 parameter settings; the lowest CFMnetwork settings (70.24%, 70.65%) lie inside P-185's interval. Whether this within-paper ablation, chained across the two papers' agreeing baselines, counts as a paper showing the explanation sufficient (a condition-3 failure) is the contested point.
performance_validity: Exclusion does not apply: P-207's highest figure (90.44% AD vs NC; 87.72% conversion) and P-185's 69.37% are below 0.97.

candidate_explanations.difference: Feature representation: ICA-network two-level coupled grey-matter volume (P-207) vs FreeSurfer AAL-region cortical thickness and volume projected into an AD/NC-learned subspace (P-185). P-207 shows its representation adds 23.6 points over plain ROI features on its own subjects, but it does not evaluate P-185's representation.
candidate_explanations.quote: The best classification accuracies for different features are 64.15% for OFMROI, 75.10% for CFMROI, 68.62% for OFMnetwork, and 87.72% for CFMnetwork.

candidate_explanations.difference: P-185's input features, for contrast with P-207's coupled GMV features.
candidate_explanations.quote: The average cortical thickness and cortical volume of each region are calculated and used as features.

candidate_explanations.difference: Parameter selection on the evaluation folds: P-207 reports the best of 15 (E1, E2) settings evaluated in the same 10-fold CV (range 70.24%-87.72%). P-185 also grid-searched its parameters, so selection is on both sides but over different grids.
candidate_explanations.quote: Here, the optimal values of E1 and E2 were searched from a small set of {2, 3, 4} and {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}, respectively.

candidate_explanations.difference: P-185's own parameter search, for contrast.
candidate_explanations.quote: Note that we also conducted the parameter optimization for each method in comparison to reach their best performance.

candidate_explanations.difference: Coupling weights (revised Pearson correlation matrices and CCA coefficients) are computed over all M subjects of the task. No within-fold estimation is described, so test subjects contribute to the feature transformation (unsupervised).
candidate_explanations.quote: Next, the Pearson's correlation coefficient, R, between each pair of the ROI-level features of ZEFM, was calculated as the network-level intra-coupled weight matrix

candidate_explanations.difference: Classifier: AdaBoost ensemble of L+1 linear-SVM base learners (P-207) vs a single linear SVM (P-185).
candidate_explanations.quote: We chose an SVM classifier with a linear kernel function as the base learner. In total, L + 1 base learners were trained

candidate_explanations.difference: Scanner and subject selection: P-207 mixes 1.5T and 3T scans with 108 MCI-nc; P-185 uses 1.5T only with 95 sMCI.
candidate_explanations.quote: The T1-weighted magnetization prepared rapid gradient echo (MPRAGE) images of all these subjects were obtained from 1.5T or 3T scanners.

candidate_explanations.difference: P-185's scanner and sample, for contrast.
candidate_explanations.quote: We use baseline MRI scans (1.5 T, 1:25 mm × 1:25 mm in-plane spatial resolution, 1.2 mm thick slices) of 528 subjects, which include 142 AD subjects, 165 NC subjects, and 221 MCI subjects. Moreover, the 221 MCI subjects contain 126 pMCI and 95 sMCI subjects.

reason: The pair meets conditions 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6. Both papers predict 3-year conversion in ADNI MCI from baseline sMRI. P-207's printed conversion accuracy (87.72%, Wilson 0.829-0.913) and P-185's 69.37% (0.630-0.751) exclude each other in both directions (two-sample z = 4.87), and the ledger's misread 90.44% does not create the gap. No figure is reported under the other paper's condition. But the two papers' plain regional-feature baselines agree (64.15% vs 62.92%), so P-207's own ablation places the gap in its coupled representation, reported at the best of 15 settings. Whether that counts as a paper showing the explanation sufficient (condition 3) is the operator's call, as in C-117. If it does not, the pair qualifies, and none of the candidate explanations is shown sufficient for the cross-paper gap.

quotes.quote: the best prediction accuracy is 90.44%, sensitivity is 88.5%, and specificity is 93.67% for AD and NC groups and the best prediction accuracy is 87.72%, sensitivity is 84.16%, and specificity is 91.64% for the MCI-c and MCI-nc groups.

This study included 121 patients with AD and 120 NC subjects, and 126 MCI converters (MCI-c) and 108 MCI non-converters (MCI-nc), with baseline structural MRI data from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) database
The patients with MCI who converted to AD within 3-year follow-up were classified into the MCI-c group; otherwise, they were classified into the MCI-nc group.
The 10-fold cross-validation was applied to evaluate the performance, and the average results were reported.
